tasks.short: Find, compare and analyse legal sources to support a lawyer's assessment.

steps.what: Define the legal question, jurisdiction, relevant dates and research limits.
Search licensed legal research services in {OTHER} for relevant authorities.
Read authorities and compare facts, legal tests and contrary interpretations.

loop.input: Retrieved source passages, research brief and authorised case facts.
loop.output: Draft comparison of relevant rules, factual distinctions and contrary authorities.
loop.check: Every legal proposition links to a source passage; paralegal checks relevance and missing counterarguments.
loop.stop: One analysis pass and one targeted correction; insufficient coverage returns an unresolved research question.
loop.why_not_simpler: Applying legal tests to differing facts requires interpretation of free text.

steps.what: Assemble the research memorandum in {DOCS}.
Verify quotations, citations and source status in legal research services in {OTHER}.
Assess the memorandum's implications and decide whether further research is needed.

tasks.design: Configure scoped retrieval in licensed legal research services in {OTHER}, then use a bounded analysis loop over retrieved passages. Deterministic templates assemble the memorandum in {DOCS}; unresolved citations block release as a checked memorandum, and the lawyer retains the legal assessment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source licensing, fragmented retrieval and contextual legal interpretation made end-to-end automation difficult.
tasks.enabler_now: Search filters, source links and document templates already exist. Bounded models can compare passages and draft analysis when constrained to retrieved material.
tasks.still_hard: Completeness, current legal status and factual distinctions remain difficult to verify. Retrieved sources do not guarantee a correct answer.
tasks.human_edge: Spot misleading analogies, seek contrary authority and judge whether the research answers the actual legal question.

ambition.what: A weekly change-of-law brief for active disputes.

tasks.altitude: The paralegal spends less time assembling memoranda and more time testing conflicting authorities. They can recommend research priorities; the lawyer retains legal conclusions and advice.

reach.task: Develop the counterargument section of a case assessment.
reach.learn: Authority hierarchy, jurisdiction, temporal applicability and material factual distinctions.

evidence.claim: Legora offers legal research, drafting and review capabilities.
An Ashurst trial reported 45% time savings on first-draft briefings; this is not an end-to-end research estimate.
A legal research benchmark reported errors on over 17% of queries, supporting substantive source checks.
Dutch professional guidance recommends checking citations by hand and protecting confidential information.

assumptions: Licensed sources provide sufficient search and retrieval access for the chosen jurisdiction.
The memorandum supports a lawyer rather than giving autonomous legal advice.
The high automation prior is reduced because substantive reading and citation verification remain substantial.
Estimates cover one practice area and jurisdiction; wider coverage needs further validation.
GDPR applies; processing arrangements and any employee consultation depend on the deployment and national rules.
unknowns: Research subscriptions, permitted reuse and available interfaces.
Languages, jurisdictions and historical source coverage required.
Who may approve a memorandum as checked and who may rely on it.
Whether the proposed change-of-law brief has an internal audience.
research_questions: Can retrieval recover known contrary authorities in representative historical matters?
How reliably do reviewers detect wrong legal status despite a valid citation?
Does source-linked analysis reduce total review time after corrections?
new_work: Review analytical drafts and verify source passages.
Maintain source access, jurisdiction filters and citation links.
Evaluate retrieval gaps and incorrect analysis on representative matters.
Update templates when legal reporting needs change.
tasks.statement: Gather and analyze research data, such as statutes, decisions, and legal articles, codes, and documents.

tasks.short: Arrange witness attendance and coordinate when witnesses are called at hearings.

steps.what: Read hearing directions and identify witness attendance requirements.

loop.output: Dates, attendance method, witness requirements, and source passages.
loop.check: Validate dates and identifiers; a paralegal checks each requirement against its source.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; missing or conflicting requirements return to manual reading.
loop.why_not_simpler: Directions contain variable free text. Structured hearing notices should bypass the loop.

steps.what: Agree the witness list and attendance approach with the lawyer.
Exchange availability and attendance details with witnesses.
Prepare witness notices using approved wording and hearing details.
Check formal notices and approve their issue.
Issue approved notices and track acknowledgements or required service evidence.
Confirm attendance and coordinate the witness call with hearing staff.

tasks.design: Configure the {WORKFLOW}, {EMAIL}, and {CALENDAR} to collect availability, track attendance, and send approved logistical messages. A bounded reader extracts hearing requirements into a case record in the {DOCS}; deterministic templates generate notices, whose issue requires lawyer approval and the correct service channel.
tasks.previous_blocker: Changing hearing directions, separate calendars, and service requirements made coordination awkward. Attendance decisions and formal notices also needed legal supervision.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling and approval features handle routine coordination. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting records and templates; bounded extraction helps with free-text directions.
tasks.still_hard: Distressed or reluctant witnesses, last-minute hearing changes, and valid service remain difficult. National procedural rules determine who may summon or call witnesses.
tasks.human_edge: A person notices hesitation, reassures witnesses without coaching testimony, and responds to hearing staff in real time.

ambition.what: A pre-hearing attendance readiness report showing missing confirmations and unresolved access needs.

tasks.altitude: The paralegal spends less time chasing replies and more time resolving attendance obstacles. They can adjust logistics within lawyer-approved limits; witness selection and formal procedural decisions remain with the lawyer.

reach.task: Prepare a source-backed witness chronology for hearing preparation.
reach.learn: Evidence relevance, hearing procedure, and the boundary between logistical support and testimony coaching.

evidence.claim: Availability collection, template filling, reminders, and acknowledgement tracking can use deterministic workflows.
Libra offers legal drafting and review. This supports document assistance, not proof of automated witness coordination.
GDPR Article 28 requires an appropriate processor contract where an external provider processes personal data on the organisation's behalf.

assumptions: This is occasional litigation support within a European company of 200 to 2,000 staff.
The paralegal acts under a lawyer's instructions; hearing staff control the courtroom call where required.
Routine availability messages can use preapproved wording and contain minimal case information.
The time split allocates more effort to email coordination than the weak mail prior suggests.
Build ranges cover one hearing workflow using existing systems and exclude unpredictable consultation or supplier delays.
unknowns: The jurisdictions, hearing types, and legally valid service channels.
Whether the company or an external lawyer manages witness attendance.
Available calendar access, witness contact permissions, and case record interfaces.
Required employee consultation under national rules and whether usage data could monitor staff.
research_questions: Which national procedural rules distinguish attendance invitations, summonses, and formal service?
Can hearing notices supply structured dates and identifiers, removing the extraction loop?
new_work: Check extracted requirements against hearing directions.
Resolve non-responses, changed dates, and inaccessible attendance arrangements.
Maintain notice templates and service-channel rules.
Check failed deliveries and keep permissioned attendance records.
tasks.statement: Call upon witnesses to testify at hearings.

tasks.short: Coordinate legal workloads, deadlines and delivery of court-required documents.

steps.what: Collect new requests and status updates from the shared {EMAIL} mailbox.
Read orders and case documents in {DOCS} to identify deadlines and dependencies.

loop.input: Court orders, case documents, verified event dates and maintained deadline rules.
loop.output: Candidate deadlines with quoted source passages, triggers and explicit calculation traces.
loop.check: Rules calculate dates; the lawyer checks operative passages, triggers and exceptions before activation.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; ambiguity or conflicting dates require manual determination.
loop.why_not_simpler: Date arithmetic is deterministic, but operative instructions and triggering events occur in free text.

steps.what: Enter verified dates and reminders in {CALENDAR}.
Resolve competing priorities and agree who handles urgent legal work.
Assign agreed work and chase progress through {PROJECT}.
Instruct an authorised service professional through {EMAIL} to deliver court-required documents.
Check returned service evidence and save it in {DOCS}.

loop.input: Service instruction, recipient details and returned service evidence.
loop.output: Draft service record with matched fields and explicit discrepancies.
loop.check: Paralegal checks source passages; legal sufficiency and disputed service go to the lawyer.
loop.stop: One extraction and comparison pass; unreadable or conflicting evidence remains unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Returned narrative evidence varies; rules can compare fields only after extraction.

tasks.design: Replace routine internal mailbox intake with a form in {WORKFLOW}, while routing exceptional correspondence to a person. A bounded extraction loop proposes deadlines from {DOCS}; approved dates populate {CALENDAR}, and agreed allocations drive tasks in {PROJECT}. Deterministic service packets require lawyer approval before dispatch, and returned evidence is checked before the service record is updated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests, calendars and service evidence were separate, while procedural dates depended on interpreting documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Forms, task rules and calendar connections handle routine coordination. A small extraction loop can expose source passages while rules handle date calculations.
tasks.still_hard: Urgent priority conflicts, procedural exceptions and valid service remain matters for people. National rules determine authorised service routes.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiate capacity, recognise escalation needs and distinguish administrative completion from legally effective service.

ambition.what: A daily deadline-risk triage deciding which matters need additional legal capacity.

tasks.altitude: The paralegal spends less time copying dates and chasing routine updates. They can recommend capacity changes from current dependencies; the lawyer retains priority and procedural decisions.

reach.task: Prepare a capacity recommendation for matters with conflicting deadlines.
reach.learn: Procedural urgency, task dependencies and the consequences of delayed service.

evidence.claim: Structured intake, calendar updates and task reminders can use configured workflows without an autonomous agent.
Legal drafting and review capabilities exist, but the digest does not establish reliable automated deadline determination.
The digest identifies Dutch works council consent requirements for individual output monitoring; national rules vary.
Court or ADR deployment can change the EU AI Act Annex III assessment.

assumptions: Subpoenas are treated as jurisdiction-specific court-required documents, not as a uniform European procedure.
Routine internal requests can move to structured intake; exceptional external correspondence still needs handling.
Only approved dates and allocations trigger downstream automation.
The design tracks matter deadlines and does not require individual productivity scoring.
GDPR applies; access review and employee consultation under national rules are included where applicable.
Estimates cover one legal team, jurisdiction and service route, with shared document and task access.
unknowns: Which deadline rules apply and who validates their maintenance.
Whether a single matter identifier links documents, dates and service instructions.
Which professionals may serve documents and what evidence they return.
Applicable employee consultation requirements and expected lead times.
Whether the deployment supports a company legal team or a court or ADR body.
research_questions: Which deadline triggers create the most ambiguity in historical files?
Can service providers return structured confirmations instead of narrative attachments?
Which alerts lead to useful capacity decisions without creating alert overload?
new_work: Review proposed deadlines and investigate source conflicts.
Maintain national procedural calendars, rules and service templates.
Handle intake exceptions, overdue work and service discrepancies.
Monitor failed synchronisation and changed document permissions.
tasks.statement: Direct and coordinate law office activity, including delivery of subpoenas.

tasks.short: Maintain current legal reference sources, subscriptions, and any retained print volumes.

steps.what: Check library catalogue holdings, subscriptions, and renewal dates.
Compare supplier edition notices with recorded holdings.
Decide which references to retain, replace, renew, or discontinue.
Place approved renewal and supplement orders.
Replace print supplements, remove superseded pages, and shelve retained volumes.
Copy completed library updates into a separate local tracking workbook.
Verify licensed reference access and flag missing or stale editions in the catalogue.

tasks.design: Configure the library catalogue in the {OTHER} to hold edition identifiers, renewal dates, and update status, then connect approved purchases through the {PROCUREMENT}. Deterministic comparisons process edition notices from the {EMAIL}, remove duplicate tracking in the {SPREADSHEET}, and produce an exception view; retained print updates remain physical work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier notices, purchase records, and local tracking were disconnected. Print handling was mixed with monitoring, making the whole task appear manual.
tasks.enabler_now: Catalogue configuration and small integrations can centralise edition and subscription metadata. No model is needed when notices contain stable identifiers; irregular notices can remain exceptions.
tasks.still_hard: Supplier metadata may be incomplete, and licences can restrict automated access. Current editions do not by themselves establish which law applies to an earlier event.
tasks.human_edge: A lawyer judges coverage needs and historical relevance. A person safely updates retained print material and resolves uncertain supplier records.

ambition.what: A legal-source coverage gap report for planned entries into new jurisdictions.

tasks.altitude: The paralegal spends less time checking notices and copying logs, and more time resolving source-access and coverage gaps. They can prioritise missing references within the approved coverage plan; subscription spending and legal coverage decisions retain their existing approval rights.

reach.task: Prepare a reference coverage brief for a new jurisdiction or legal topic.
reach.learn: Source authority, historical versions, licence limits, and the team's planned legal needs.

evidence.claim: Catalogue fields, renewal reminders, edition comparisons, and duplicate-log removal can use configuration and deterministic code.
The digest's legal research benchmark reports errors on over 17% of tested queries; catalogue currency should not be treated as validated legal advice.
In the Netherlands, employee monitoring arrangements may require works council consent under WOR Article 27; this design does not need individual output tracking.

assumptions: A mid-size corporate legal team primarily uses licensed digital references and retains a small print collection.
The library catalogue is a library-management category represented by the {OTHER}.
A separate local update workbook duplicates catalogue information and can be removed.
Edition identifiers are available for routine notices; unparseable notices receive manual review.
The digital emphasis differs from the prior's large in-person share; retained print work remains manual.
Build ranges cover existing catalogue and procurement access, including consultation assessment; reference subscription costs are excluded.
unknowns: Whether a maintained print library or duplicate update workbook exists.
The catalogue's configuration options and supplier metadata interfaces.
Licence restrictions on automated access checks.
The required historical holdings and legal coverage priorities.
Purchasing authority and any employee consultation required under national rules.
research_questions: Can suppliers provide structured edition and renewal metadata?
Which retained print sources have acceptable licensed digital equivalents?
How should historical editions be labelled so they remain available without appearing current?
new_work: Resolve unrecognised edition notices and broken source access.
Maintain supplier identifiers and catalogue mappings.
Review coverage gaps with lawyers.
Record completion of retained print updates in the catalogue.
Maintain a single update record after retiring the duplicate workbook.
tasks.statement: Keep and monitor legal volumes to ensure that the law library is up-to-date.

tasks.short: Compile an estate asset inventory and support defensible property valuations.

steps.what: Request asset evidence from the estate representative and relevant custodians.
Record reported assets, ownership, balances, and supporting document references.

loop.input: Asset statements, ownership documents, and item lists.
loop.output: Asset records with owner, reported value, currency, date, and source location.
loop.check: Validate types and totals; check ownership, valuation dates, and every material amount against the source.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; conflicting ownership or amounts require manual entry.
loop.why_not_simpler: Evidence arrives in varied free-text documents. Structured statements should be imported directly.

steps.what: Verify property ownership and account balances against authorised records.
Inspect accessible property and record condition, identity, and missing items.
Agree valuation dates, evidence standards, and the need for specialist appraisals.
Assess valuation evidence and specialist reports against the agreed basis.
Consolidate the inventory and obtain approval of the final version.

tasks.design: A permissioned asset register in the {WORKFLOW} links each holding to evidence in the {DOCS}, with authorised imports from the {BANK} and {GOV_PORTAL}. A bounded reader proposes fields from documents, while deterministic checks detect duplicates and calculate totals; final inventory approval stays with the lawyer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Asset evidence arrived in inconsistent documents and valuations used different dates or ownership assumptions. Physical condition and specialist judgement were never suitable for simple automation.
tasks.enabler_now: A small records app can preserve evidence, dates, currencies, and exceptions without repeated spreadsheet assembly. Bounded extraction reduces transcription effort rather than supplying unsupported valuations.
tasks.still_hard: Hidden assets, disputed ownership, illiquid holdings, and unusual personal property need investigation. Specialist appraisals and national succession or tax rules remain expensive.
tasks.human_edge: A person assesses physical condition, notices incomplete disclosure, and distinguishes a reported price from a defensible valuation.

ambition.what: A pre-meeting estate liquidity and missing-evidence report.

tasks.altitude: The paralegal spends less time transcribing statements and more time investigating ownership and valuation gaps. They can prioritise evidence collection and recommend specialist appraisal; legal and tax conclusions remain with qualified advisers.

reach.task: Prepare an asset liquidity and ownership-restriction brief for estate planning.
reach.learn: Valuation bases, succession terminology, liquidity limits, and the separation of factual support from legal or tax advice.

evidence.claim: Asset registers, duplicate checks, dated values, inventory templates, and arithmetic can use deterministic technology.
Legora offers legal drafting and review. The digest does not establish automated estate valuation.
Kadaster demonstrates deed extraction with human confirmation of flagged easements; this is adjacent evidence for document handling.
An external processor handling personal asset evidence needs an appropriate GDPR Article 28 contract.

assumptions: Estate planning is uncommon in a general corporate legal team. This describes the task where an estate, fiduciary, or private-client remit exists.
The paralegal supports appraisal and commissions qualified specialists where required.
Asset holders have authorised access to statements and registry records.
Currency conversions use an approved rate source and valuation date.
Build ranges cover a limited asset register and existing authorised sources, excluding specialist appraisal fees and elapsed appointment time.
unknowns: Whether estate planning is actually performed by this company's legal team.
Asset classes, estate jurisdictions, and the required valuation standard.
Access rights to bank and registry information.
Who may commission appraisals and approve the inventory.
Required retention periods and employee consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which asset classes require independent or formally qualified appraisals under the applicable national rules?
Which statement formats can be imported without a model?
What evidence supports the chosen valuation date and currency conversion basis?
new_work: Review extracted asset records and source references.
Resolve duplicates, ownership conflicts, and stale balances.
Maintain asset categories and valuation-date checks.
Track missing appraisals and preserve valuation provenance.
Review access permissions and evidence retention.
tasks.statement: Appraise and inventory real and personal property for estate planning.

tasks.short: Prepare routine legal documents and correspondence, obtain approval, and maintain the matter file.

steps.what: Read instructions and collect supporting documents.

loop.output: Document request with source-linked fields and missing information.
loop.check: Validate required fields; show each extracted fact beside its source.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; unresolved fields go to the paralegal.
loop.why_not_simpler: An intake form handles structured requests; existing narrative instructions still require reading.

steps.what: Check names, dates, matter references, and missing facts.
Populate a precedent and draft case-specific wording.

loop.input: Verified facts, approved precedent, and selected source passages.
loop.output: Routine document draft with factual source references.
loop.check: Lock standard wording; validate populated fields; flag unsupported statements.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass; missing evidence produces a placeholder.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle standard wording; case-specific narrative cannot always be expressed as field substitutions.

steps.what: Review legal wording and decide whether the document is ready.
Resolve factual corrections with the declarant or business contact.
Obtain release approval and send correspondence or arrange execution.
Name, index, and file the final document and receipt.

tasks.design: Configure matter metadata, precedents, versioning, and filing in the {DOCS}, with requests and release approvals in the {WORKFLOW}. A bounded loop extracts narrative instructions and drafts variable passages; deterministic checks validate fields before approved dispatch through the {EMAIL} or execution through the {ESIGN}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Narrative requests, inconsistent precedents, and disconnected filing made simple mail merges insufficient. Confidentiality and execution requirements also limited reuse.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing templates and approval features cover much of the task. AI-assisted coding can reduce connector development effort; bounded extraction handles the remaining narrative inputs.
tasks.still_hard: Confirming disputed facts, protecting confidentiality, and meeting jurisdiction-specific execution requirements. Electronic signing does not satisfy every affidavit formality.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when a declarant is uncertain, a statement overreaches, or routine correspondence carries an unintended legal commitment.

ambition.what: Routine legal correspondence clinic for business teams.

tasks.altitude: The paralegal spends less time copying facts and filing versions, and more time resolving incomplete instructions. They gain delegated authority to return incomplete requests and select approved routine templates; lawyers retain legal release authority.

reach.task: Prepare a first issue list for routine correspondence.
reach.learn: Distinguish factual assertions, legal conclusions, and commitments requiring legal approval.

evidence.claim: Libra and Legora offer legal drafting and review capabilities; this supports capability availability, not unattended release.
Ashurst reported 80% time savings on corporate filings in its trial; that result does not establish savings for affidavits.
Templates, metadata validation, approved dispatch, and automatic filing can handle routine document administration.
GDPR Article 28 requires appropriate processor terms when a processor handles personal data.

assumptions: The baseline is an in-house legal team serving a European company with 200 to 2,000 staff.
Routine documents use reusable precedents; substantive drafting is covered separately.
Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured savings.
Build ranges cover one document family; access work may overlap development.
GDPR applies. EU AI Act obligations depend on the actual use; national rules govern execution formalities and employee consultation.
unknowns: Which precedents are approved and who may authorise release?
Which documents require witnesses, notarisation, originals, or physical filing?
Can the existing document store enforce matter access and retention?
Does rollout trigger consultation under applicable national rules?
research_questions: Which document families can be generated entirely from structured intake?
Which execution routes are valid for the selected jurisdictions?
new_work: Review extracted facts and unsupported draft passages.
Maintain precedents, required fields, and recipient rules.
Handle dispatch failures, execution exceptions, and filing conflicts.
Periodically inspect access controls and retention behaviour.
tasks.statement: Prepare affidavits or other documents, such as legal correspondence, and organize and maintain documents in paper or electronic filing system.

tasks.short: Prepare trial exhibits, hearing bundles, and logistics with the lawyer.

steps.what: Agree hearing requirements, responsibilities, and the exhibit plan.
Collect requested exhibits and track missing versions or originals.
Map exhibits to issues and propose their sequence.
Number exhibits, paginate files, and create the bundle index.
Review exhibit selection, privilege, redactions, and procedural compliance.
Prepare required paper copies, labels, and original exhibits.
Rehearse exhibit retrieval and resolve hearing logistics with the lawyer.
Obtain release approval and deliver the required bundle.

tasks.design: Configure an exhibit register and missing-item queue in the {DOCS} and {PROJECT}, then generate pagination, bookmarks, and indexes deterministically on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. Lawyers retain exhibit and privilege decisions, while the {WORKFLOW} controls release of the exact final bundle through the {EMAIL} or {GOV_PORTAL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Late exhibit changes, variable hearing specifications, and mixed physical and digital evidence made generic bundle assembly unreliable. Judgement-heavy preparation also obscured the separable clerical work.
tasks.enabler_now: Version control, fixed manifests, document transformation libraries, and configured work queues can automate administration. No model loop is necessary for the proposed first release.
tasks.still_hard: Exhibit relevance, privilege, procedural exceptions, originals, and last-minute strategy changes. Physical preparation and rehearsal remain substantial.
tasks.human_edge: Anticipating what the lawyer will need under pressure, preserving evidence context, and noticing a missing or misleading exhibit.

ambition.what: Pre-hearing evidence-readiness review for external counsel.

tasks.altitude: The paralegal spends less time rebuilding indexes and more time resolving evidence gaps and rehearsing retrieval. They gain delegated authority to enforce bundle specifications and request missing materials; lawyers retain exhibit selection and release decisions.

reach.task: Prepare an issue-to-exhibit gap review before the hearing.
reach.learn: Understand evidential relevance, privilege, authenticity, and procedural requirements.

evidence.claim: Exhibit numbering, pagination, indexing, duplicate detection, and manifest checks can be implemented deterministically.
A work queue can separate missing-item coordination from legal exhibit decisions.
The digest provides no documented trial-bundle case or measured savings for this proposed workflow.

assumptions: The company has occasional litigation, with an internal or external lawyer directing preparation.
This baseline includes some required paper copies or originals; all-digital hearings change the time split.
The source documents are already digitised; conversion of legacy archives is outside the build estimate.
Portal uploads remain manual where supported configuration is unavailable.
The human-heavy prior remains credible for legal selection and rehearsal, while assembly is separately automatable.
GDPR applies. EU AI Act obligations depend on any later model use; national rules govern procedure, evidence handling, and employee consultation.

How often are physical copies or original exhibits required?
Who decides privilege, redactions, and final exhibit selection?
What electronic delivery routes and size limits apply?
What local access approval and employee consultation are required?

Can the generator preserve required signatures, redactions, bookmarks, and document integrity?
Which late changes cause the most assembly rework?
new_work: Maintain bundle specifications and venue checklists.
Resolve duplicate, missing-version, and unreadable-file exceptions.
Verify redactions and inspect generated bundles before release.
Check delivery receipts and manage replacement bundles.
Maintain permissions and retention for hearing materials.
tasks.statement: Prepare for trial by performing tasks such as organizing exhibits.

tasks.short: Meet clients and professionals to clarify case facts, open questions and next steps.

steps.what: Arrange the case meeting through {EMAIL} and check availability in {CALENDAR}.
Read the case file in {DOCS} and prepare questions.

loop.input: Authorised case documents, meeting purpose and a fixed question template.
loop.output: Draft meeting brief with source references and unresolved factual questions.
loop.check: Paralegal checks material facts against linked passages and removes unsupported questions.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; missing sources remain flagged for manual preparation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates organise the brief, but relevant facts and contradictions occur in free text.

steps.what: Discuss facts, clarify uncertainty and agree permissible next steps with participants.
Turn meeting notes into a case note in {DOCS}.

loop.input: Contemporaneous meeting notes and the case-note template.
loop.output: Draft case note separating reported facts, uncertainties and proposed actions.
loop.check: Paralegal checks attribution, omissions and commitments before saving the approved record.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unclear statements return to the paralegal.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes need careful rewriting; a template alone cannot preserve their meaning.

steps.what: Record owners and follow-up dates in {PROJECT}; flag legal decisions for the lawyer.

tasks.design: Configure scheduling in {CALENDAR} and generate a source-linked meeting brief from authorised documents in {DOCS}. After the human conversation, a bounded drafting loop turns notes into a reviewed case record; {WORKFLOW} creates tasks in {PROJECT} and routes legal decisions to the lawyer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Case information is scattered, and preparing useful questions requires reading confidential narrative documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling features handle coordination. Bounded drafting can prepare briefs and notes within controlled document access.
tasks.still_hard: Trust, conflicting accounts and sensitive disclosures require a person. Confidentiality, GDPR and national rules constrain data handling.
tasks.human_edge: Build rapport, notice hesitation, ask useful follow-up questions and recognise when a lawyer must intervene.
tasks.altitude: The week contains less scheduling and note rewriting, with more time to clarify disputed facts. Legal decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Prepare a factual chronology and identify gaps before a case conference.
reach.learn: Distinguish reported facts, evidence, legal conclusions and privileged material.

evidence.claim: Legal research, drafting and review products exist; this supports bounded briefing assistance.
Scheduling and action creation can use configured rules; the conversation remains human.
GDPR Article 28 governs processor arrangements when an external processor handles personal data.

assumptions: The baseline is an internal legal team supporting a mid-size European company.
Meetings use calls or in-person discussion; preparation uses documents rather than spreadsheets.
The design uses written notes and does not require recording conversations.
Build estimates assume existing document access and scheduling interfaces; consultation time varies under national rules.
unknowns: Which matters the paralegal may discuss without a lawyer present.
Document permissions, retention rules and approved processing arrangements.
Whether existing scheduling and task features are enabled.
research_questions: Which brief format helps participants resolve factual uncertainty fastest?
How often do drafted notes omit a qualification or misattribute a statement?
new_work: Check briefs and case notes against their sources.
Resolve ambiguous actions and route legal decisions.
Maintain templates, permissions and integration mappings.
tasks.statement: Meet with clients and other professionals to discuss details of cases.

tasks.short: Prepare approved pleadings, submit them through the permitted court channel and preserve filing evidence.

steps.what: Assemble pleadings, exhibits and filing forms from {DOCS}.
Check the filing package against the court's procedural checklist.
Approve the exact package, court, case reference and submission timing.
Submit the authorised package through the court's {GOV_PORTAL}.
Retrieve the court receipt or rejection notice from {GOV_PORTAL}.
Save filing evidence in {DOCS}, update {PROJECT} and flag rejected submissions.

tasks.design: A deterministic generator assembles the filing package from {DOCS}, checks formal requirements and records the lawyer's approval in {WORKFLOW}. The paralegal submits through {GOV_PORTAL} using that same approval, then attaches the receipt; {WORKFLOW} stores evidence and updates {PROJECT}. Any package change invalidates the approval, and an upload alone never counts as an accepted filing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Court-specific formats, restricted submission channels and exact-version approval requirements left preparation and filing disconnected.
tasks.enabler_now: Document assembly, file validation and version-bound approvals need ordinary code and configuration. Submission can remain manual while its preparation and records improve.
tasks.still_hard: National procedural rules, filing rights, portal credentials and receipt meanings vary. A rejected or late filing requires prompt human judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Confirm procedural suitability, detect substantive omissions and respond to a rejection before the deadline.
tasks.altitude: The paralegal assembles fewer bundles and chases fewer filing records. Filing authority and legal decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Prepare a procedural readiness assessment before filing.
reach.learn: Court-specific formalities, authority to file and the distinction between submission and acceptance.

evidence.claim: Bundle assembly, formal validation and version-bound approvals can use deterministic technology.
The digest documents a Dutch case imposing full costs after unchecked AI-drafted pleadings.
The digest provides no evidence of a court filing integration; portal automation is not assumed.

assumptions: The illustrated route permits electronic filing by authorised legal support staff.
Where external counsel must file, the submission handoff changes to that role.
Paper or in-person routes remain manual under national rules.
The means prior is adjusted toward portal filing for this baseline; local practice must confirm it.
Estimates cover one court route and exclude automating its submission portal.
GDPR applies to case records; access and any consultation requirements follow the deployment and national rules.
unknowns: Whether the company files directly or instructs external counsel.
Permitted channels, authentication requirements and delegated filing rights.
Applicable package formats, size limits and receipt semantics.
Who monitors rejection notices and approaching deadlines.
research_questions: Which formal defects account for repeated filing rework?
Can receipt attachment reliably distinguish acceptance, pending processing and rejection?
new_work: Maintain procedural checklists and document-format rules.
Review validation exceptions and approve exact package versions.
Monitor missing receipts and route rejections urgently.
Retest templates when court requirements change.

tasks.short: Review property closing evidence and help parties resolve disputes under legal supervision.

steps.what: Collect the transaction documents and parties' stated concerns.
Retrieve current property registry records using the property's identifiers.
Compare title documents, registry entries, ownership details, and restrictions.

loop.input: Title documents, registry records, and property identifiers.
loop.output: Source-linked ownership and restriction fields for deterministic comparison.
loop.check: Match identifiers, names, dates, and amounts; a person checks every extracted restriction against the original.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; unreadable pages or unmatched fields enter the exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Historical deeds contain free-text restrictions. Structured registry fields should use direct comparisons.

steps.what: Prepare a discrepancy brief with supporting passages and missing documents.
Assess legal significance and agree the permitted negotiation position.
Help parties clarify issues and record possible settlement terms.
Reconcile closing figures and assemble the closing packet.
Review the closing packet and authorise its release.
Send the authorised closing packet and retain delivery evidence.

tasks.design: A case record in the {WORKFLOW} links documents in the {DOCS} to authorised registry queries through the {GOV_PORTAL}. A bounded extraction loop supplies source-linked fields for deterministic comparisons and closing calculations; the {EMAIL} releases only the packet version approved by the lawyer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Registry access, scanned deeds, and closing figures lived in separate places. Legal significance and disputed terms could not be reduced to reliable checklist rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured identifiers and repeatable calculations support deterministic checks. Bounded document extraction and faster integration development reduce preparation effort without changing legal authority.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous restrictions, incomplete title history, and contested facts require legal judgement. Binding arbitration, conveyancing authority, and registration requirements depend on national rules and the appointed professionals.
tasks.human_edge: The lawyer assesses enforceability and risk. The paralegal helps parties explain concerns and preserves an accurate record of what remains unresolved.

ambition.what: An early closing-readiness review before the company commits to a transaction timetable.

tasks.altitude: The paralegal spends more of the week investigating exceptions and coordinating missing evidence. They can prioritise evidence requests and recommend escalation; settlement commitments and closing release remain with authorised decision-makers.

reach.task: Prepare alternative ways to satisfy a disputed closing condition.
reach.learn: Property rights, contractual remedies, evidence provenance, and the limits of delegated negotiation.

evidence.claim: Structured comparisons, closing arithmetic, document checklists, and release controls can use deterministic code.
Kadaster AkteAI combines models and rules to extract deed data. This supports extraction feasibility, not automated dispute resolution.
Kadaster's historical-deed processing flags easements for human confirmation.
Qualia Clear drafts preliminary title exams and proposes curative tasks in the US title context.
The AEGIS Land Title vendor case reports about 10 to 20 commitments daily and a full audit of each file; no period is given.
EU AI Act Annex III includes relevant justice uses when performed for a court or ADR body; ordinary corporate legal support is not automatically covered by that category.

assumptions: The company occasionally acquires, sells, or disputes rights in property.
The paralegal supports negotiation and closing; they do not independently make a binding arbitral award.
Registry records can be obtained through a permitted interface or authorised structured exports.
A spreadsheet currently reconciles closing figures; registry searching itself uses a system.
Build ranges cover a pilot for one jurisdiction and document family; external professional fees are excluded.
unknowns: The applicable property jurisdiction and required notarial or conveyancing involvement.
Whether formal arbitration is actually part of this role and who has authority to decide.
Registry access rights, charges, export formats, and freshness requirements.
The closing document types, approval thresholds, and settlement authority.
Whether processing is on behalf of a court or ADR body.
Required employee consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which registry fields and deed exchanges are available in structured form?
Which closing conditions can be mechanically checked in the selected jurisdiction?
Does any proposed deployment fall within the EU AI Act's court or ADR use category?
new_work: Confirm extracted ownership and restriction passages.
Investigate mismatches and missing registry evidence.
Maintain jurisdiction-specific closing templates and calculation rules.
Control approved packet versions and recipient permissions.
Monitor registry interface changes and extraction failures.
tasks.statement: Arbitrate disputes between parties and assist in the real estate closing process, such as by reviewing title searches.

tasks.short: Investigate case facts and legal authorities, then prepare a verified research briefing for a lawyer.

steps.what: Agree the research question, jurisdiction, relevant dates, and factual uncertainties.
Search legal research databases, public registers, and the matter file.
Check source relevance, jurisdiction, authority, and currency.
Extract material facts, dates, holdings, and conflicting evidence.

loop.input: Verified source pack and supporting documents.
loop.output: Fact chronology and authority table with quotations and source locations.
loop.check: Match quotations to source text; mark allegations, findings, and conflicting dates separately.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per source; unresolved conflicts go to the paralegal.
loop.why_not_simpler: Dates can be parsed by rules, but their meaning and the distinction between allegations and findings require reading.

steps.what: Write a research briefing addressing the question and evidence gaps.

loop.input: Research brief, reviewed chronology, and verified authority passages.
loop.output: Research draft with supported propositions, contrary authority, and open questions.
loop.check: Require source references for legal propositions; block unsupported citations and flag uncertain conclusions.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass; unresolved citations block delivery as a verified briefing.
loop.why_not_simpler: The briefing must connect facts with varied legal texts; fixed templates only provide its structure.

steps.what: Open cited sources and verify quotations and the propositions they support.
Assess possible causes of action and decide further investigation.

tasks.design: Configure saved searches in the legal research database, represented by the {OTHER}, and keep a source register in the {DOCS}. A controlled answer desk on the {DATA_PLATFORM} extracts chronology and drafts briefings from selected sources, with deterministic citation checks and human verification before a lawyer uses the findings.
tasks.previous_blocker: Research depends on source licences, changing law, incomplete facts, and context-sensitive relevance. Keyword search alone cannot produce a reliable case briefing.
tasks.enabler_now: Saved searches and source registers already reduce repeated retrieval. Bounded extraction and drafting can turn selected materials into reviewable work, without delegating open-ended investigation.
tasks.still_hard: Finding omitted authorities, establishing whether law remains current, and distinguishing persuasive text from legally relevant support. Source access may require separate licences or unsupported manual retrieval.
tasks.human_edge: Formulating the right question, recognising missing evidence, and testing a preferred theory against contrary facts and authorities.

ambition.what: Early dispute viability briefing before escalation to external counsel.

tasks.altitude: The paralegal spends less time assembling quotations and more time testing evidence gaps. They gain delegated authority to organise the research plan and request factual clarification; lawyers retain legal conclusions and litigation decisions.

reach.task: Prepare a preliminary causes-of-action and evidence-gap matrix.
reach.learn: Map legal elements, limitation issues, burdens of proof, and adverse authority.

evidence.claim: Libra offers legal research capabilities.
The cited benchmark found errors on over 17% of queries for evaluated legal research tools; this is not a universal tool error rate.
Dutch professional guidance recommends checking citations manually; this is national guidance, not an EU-wide professional rule.
Retrieval logs, exact quotation checks, and source-linked extraction can support a bounded research workflow.

assumptions: The company has recurring disputes or investigations that justify an internal research workflow.
The {OTHER} denotes a licensed legal research database, not an unrestricted web search service.
The baseline includes manual searches and document reading; API access is not assumed.
Integration estimates exclude purchasing source licences and creating unsupported access methods.
GDPR applies to case materials. EU AI Act Annex III assessment depends on purpose; work for courts or ADR bodies needs separate assessment.
National rules govern professional confidentiality and any required employee consultation.
unknowns: Which jurisdictions and source collections must research cover?
What retrieval, storage, and model-processing rights do source licences allow?
Who may certify a briefing as verified?
Are investigations likely to include special-category personal data?
What access controls and consultation steps are required locally?
research_questions: Which source collections expose reliable current-status information?
Can a pilot detect adverse authority and evidence gaps as reliably as the present process?
Which research requests are narrow enough for a fixed source and time budget?
new_work: Maintain source permissions and retrieval connectors.
Verify quotations, legal propositions, and source currency.
Investigate blocked citations and contradictory evidence.
Sample briefings for omitted adverse authority.
Update extraction guidance when recurring classification errors appear.
tasks.statement: Investigate facts and law of cases and search pertinent sources, such as public records and internet sources, to determine causes of action and to prepare cases.

tasks.short: Draft and revise substantive legal documents for lawyer review and authorised release.

steps.what: Clarify the document purpose, jurisdiction, deadline, and legal instructions.
Collect precedents, source documents, and any financial schedules.
Identify factual gaps, clause choices, and departures from the precedent.

loop.input: Drafting pack, approved clause guidance, and drafting brief.
loop.output: Source-linked gaps, deviations, and proposed clause options.
loop.check: Check checklist coverage; require exact passages for every alleged deviation.
loop.stop: One comparison and one repair pass; unresolved legal choices remain open.
loop.why_not_simpler: Exact comparisons handle standard clauses, but negotiated wording can express equivalent or conflicting obligations.

steps.what: Prepare the first draft and calculate schedules where required.

loop.input: Approved precedent, reviewed issue list, and source-linked facts.
loop.output: Legal document draft with marked variable passages and unresolved points.
loop.check: Validate fields, cross-references, and source support; calculate financial schedules deterministically.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass; unsupported arguments remain flagged for a person.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates and arithmetic cover standard material; bespoke arguments and negotiated clauses require language generation.

steps.what: Check citations, definitions, amounts, cross-references, and consistency.
Resolve legal choices and revise arguments, obligations, or remedies.
Obtain release approval, issue the document, and save the final version.

tasks.design: Use approved precedents in the {DOCS}, structured instructions in the {WORKFLOW}, and controlled financial inputs from the {ERP}. Deterministic generators handle fields, schedules, and cross-references; bounded loops compare clauses and draft variable passages, with lawyer approval before release through the {EMAIL}, {ESIGN}, or {GOV_PORTAL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Legal document types vary widely, and precedent quality is uneven. Conventional assembly tools struggle with negotiated language and case-specific arguments.
tasks.enabler_now: Document assembly and arithmetic already work deterministically. Bounded language models can assist comparison and first drafting, while AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting these parts.
tasks.still_hard: Legal strategy, enforceability, conflicting evidence, and changing law still demand qualified judgement. Mechanical citation matching cannot establish that an authority supports an argument.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing which obligations or arguments serve the matter, and recognising when a plausible draft creates unacceptable exposure.

ambition.what: Pre-negotiation clause options briefing for business owners.

tasks.altitude: The paralegal spends more of the week comparing options and resolving factual gaps. They gain delegated authority to apply approved drafting options within a written playbook; lawyers retain substantive legal decisions and release authority.

reach.task: Prepare a clause options briefing before negotiation.
reach.learn: Explain legal and commercial consequences, precedent limits, and escalation thresholds.

evidence.claim: Legora offers legal drafting and review capabilities.
Ashurst reported 45% time savings on first-draft briefings in its trial; this is not a benchmark for all legal documents.
Document templates and deterministic arithmetic can generate standard clauses, populated fields, and closing schedules.
The digest records a Dutch case involving unchecked AI-drafted pleadings and a full-costs consequence.

assumptions: Most in-house work concerns contracts, correspondence, and dispute drafts; specialist instruments involve qualified external support.
Financial schedules apply only to relevant document types.
Collection automation uses an explicit source manifest and existing permissions.
Portal transmission remains manual where no supported automation exists; the remaining-time estimate includes that work.
Build ranges cover one substantive document family, not every instrument listed in the occupational description.
GDPR applies; EU AI Act classification follows the deployment context. National rules govern professional duties, execution, filing, and consultation.
unknowns: Which document family has sufficient repeat volume and approved precedents?
Which clause decisions can be delegated to a paralegal?
Which financial inputs have an authoritative source?
Which filing channels support controlled submission?
What access, processor terms, and national consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Which drafting choices can be captured as explicit rules?
How often do precedent deviations require legal escalation?
What quality threshold should a pilot meet before expanding to another document family?
new_work: Review proposed clause classifications and generated passages.
Maintain approved precedents and clause guidance.
Verify legal citations and substantive use of authorities.
Investigate inconsistent calculations and failed submissions.
Revalidate generation rules after precedent changes.
tasks.statement: Prepare, edit, or review legal documents, including legislation, briefs, pleadings, appeals, wills, contracts, and real estate closing statements.

role_batches.altitude: The role moves from document assembly toward evidence quality, drafting options, and hearing readiness. Delegated rights can expand within approved playbooks, while lawyers retain legal strategy, substantive advice, and external release decisions.
reach: Lawyer: prepare clause options and explain escalation points.
Lawyer: map possible causes of action to verified facts and evidence gaps.
Lawyer: prepare an issue-to-exhibit readiness review.
skills_to_grow: Source verification and legal research methods.
Evidence provenance, privilege, and redaction review.
Confidential data handling and access control.
Clear explanation of uncertainty and escalation.
role_batches.ambitious_version: A legal operations and case-preparation specialist who delivers verified drafting packs, early dispute briefings, and hearing-readiness reviews, with explicit delegated authority and lawyer accountability for legal decisions.

role_batches.altitude: The role shifts toward factual quality, procedural readiness and exception handling, with less document assembly and coordination. Paralegals gain stronger grounds to recommend research and capacity priorities; legal advice, strategy and procedural authorisations stay with the lawyer.
reach: Prepare counterargument analysis for a lawyer's case assessment.
Produce procedural readiness assessments before filing.
Recommend capacity changes when case deadlines conflict.
skills_to_grow: Source verification and detection of misleading legal analogies.
Clear separation of facts, allegations, evidence and legal conclusions.
Procedural deadline validation and service requirements.
Confidential document access, GDPR and privilege handling.
Workflow exception diagnosis and template maintenance.
role_batches.ambitious_version: A legal operations partner who brings lawyers current evidence, tested counterarguments and clear procedural risks, enabling earlier decisions on active matters.

role_batches.altitude: The paralegal's week shifts toward evidence quality, exceptions, and practical support for people involved in legal matters. They gain bounded authority to prioritise evidence requests and logistics; legal advice, binding settlements, and formal procedural authority remain with authorised professionals.
reach: Prepare source-backed witness chronologies for a lawyer's hearing preparation.
Develop evidence-backed options for disputed closing conditions.
Prepare estate liquidity and ownership briefs where estate work is genuinely within scope.
Identify legal reference coverage gaps for planned jurisdiction changes.
skills_to_grow: Document extraction review and exception handling.
Registry access, confidentiality, and GDPR responsibilities.
National procedural boundaries and effective communication with witnesses and parties.
role_batches.ambitious_version: A legal readiness service gives lawyers early visibility of attendance obstacles, missing closing evidence, unsupported asset values, and reference coverage gaps. It uses permissioned records, deterministic checks, and small reviewed extraction loops; professional decisions and sensitive conversations remain human.
